extraction.name: DocVQA
extraction.description: A dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images, consisting of 50,000 questions defined on 12,000+ document images. The dataset includes varied document types (e.g., tables, forms, figures) and requires models to interpret text within the layout/structure of the document, not just extract text. Answers are open-ended and not sourced from a closed dictionary.
extraction.creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar
extraction.publisher: CVIT, IIIT Hyderabad, India; Computer Vision Center, UAB, Spain
extraction.citeAs: DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Document images sourced from UCSF Industry Documents Library, spanning 6,071 documents from 1900 to 2018 across 5 industries (tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, chemical). Images include typewritten, printed, handwritten, and born-digital text, with prioritization for pages containing tables, forms, lists, and figures. Questions and answers collected via remote workers using a web-based annotation tool in a three-stage process: (1) workers define up to 10 question-answer pairs per image, (2) verification of collected data with question type tagging, and (3) review of mismatched answers by authors.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: OCR tokens extracted using a commercial OCR solution. Document images binarized in the source library, but efforts made to minimize binarized images in DocVQA to avoid image quality bottlenecks. OCR tokens serialized into a single string in top-left to bottom-right order for model input.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three-stage annotation process: (1) Workers define up to 10 question-answer pairs per image, encouraged to add multiple ground truth answers where warranted. Workers instructed to ask questions answerable from text in the image and enter answers verbatim. (2) Verification stage where workers enter answers for questions (without seeing first-stage answers) and assign one or more question types to each question. Questions flagged for language issues or ambiguity are excluded. (3) Review stage for questions where first-stage and second-stage answers do not match, handled by authors who edit or accept/reject questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Questions tagged with 9 types based on reasoning requirements (e.g., form, layout, table/list, running text, handwritten, photograph, figure, yes/no, other). Analysis includes comparison of question/answer lengths, OCR token statistics, and question type distributions. Human performance benchmarked at 94.36% accuracy.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Up to 10 question-answer pairs per document image in the first annotation stage, with multiple ground truth answers allowed where warranted.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Commercial OCR solution for text extraction
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Dataset, code, and leaderboard available at docvqa.org. Versioning implied by split ratios (80:10:10 train/validation/test) and ongoing maintenance of the leaderboard.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Potentially includes names of individuals, institutions, and places (e.g., 'Dr. William J. Darby', 'American Heart Association') in answers and document content.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Dataset aims to inspire 'purpose-driven' document image analysis research, addressing practical needs in document understanding. Highlights importance of interpreting text within document structure/layout, which has implications for accessibility, automation, and information retrieval in real-world documents.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Potential biases include: (1) Overrepresentation of certain industries (e.g., food/nutrition) due to availability of non-binarized images. (2) Temporal bias toward 1960-2000 period. (3) Document type imbalance (e.g., higher representation of reports/invoices leading to numeric answer dominance). (4) Language bias toward English and common question patterns (e.g., 'what is the date...'). (5) OCR errors may introduce systematic biases in answers.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Known limitations include: (1) Generalization limits due to domain-specific document types (e.g., tables, forms). (2) Quality issues from binarized source images. (3) Heavy reliance on OCR accuracy for answer extraction. (4) Performance gap between models and human accuracy (94.36%), particularly for questions requiring document structure understanding. (5) Non-recommended uses include applications requiring high precision in numeric/date extraction without OCR error handling.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, and Fine-Tuning for Visual Question Answering (VQA) models on document images. Usage guidelines emphasize the need for models to interpret text within document layout/structure, not just extract text. Recommended for research in document image analysis, multimodal learning, and reading comprehension systems.
